html: The Dene Tha' are a Dene First Nation of north-western Alberta, Canada, around the Hay River and its lakes. They speak South Slavey, an Athabaskan language, close to that of the Dehcho Dene to the north. They lived by hunting moose, caribou and beaver, fishing and trapping furs for the Hudson's Bay Company. In 1900 they joined Treaty 8, and their main communities today are Chateh (Assumption), Meander River and Bushe River. Oil and gas wells have spread across much of their land since the mid 1900s. Their southern neighbours were the Dane-zaa.
